title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether ChatGPT improves student learning outcomes and under what conditions its effects are strongest. The authors synthesize experimental and quasi-experimental studies published from November 2022 to February 2025, focusing on three outcomes: learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking. The motivation is that prior primary studies and reviews have reported mixed findings, so a meta-analysis is needed to estimate overall effects and identify moderators.

The intervention studied is the use of ChatGPT as a learning support tool in education. Across the included studies, ChatGPT was used in a variety of ways, including as an intelligent tutor, intelligent partner, or intelligent learning tool, and within several learning models such as personalized learning, problem-based learning, project-based learning, contextual learning, and reflective learning. The paper reports evidence from 51 studies with 72 independent effect sizes, spanning primary, secondary, and college settings, although almost all evidence came from college samples.

The findings show that ChatGPT has a large positive effect on learning performance and moderate positive effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking. Moderator analyses suggest that effects on performance vary by course type, learning model, and duration; performance is strongest in skills/competencies courses, problem-based learning, and interventions lasting 4–8 weeks. Learning perception is mainly moderated by duration, with longer interventions producing larger effects. For higher-order thinking, course type and the role of ChatGPT matter, with the strongest effects when ChatGPT functions as an intelligent tutor. Overall, the paper concludes that ChatGPT can be beneficial in education, especially when paired with structured scaffolds and used over a sustained period.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis of 51 experimental/quasi-experimental studies with explicit inclusion criteria, effect-size calculation, heterogeneity tests, publication-bias checks, and sensitivity analyses. That makes it high on credibility, though the evidence is not fully K-12-specific and includes a large college share.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effects are medium to large, especially for learning performance (g=0.867) and higher-order thinking (g=0.457). Even though the review is broader than K-12 science instruction, the magnitude and consistency of positive effects support a blue impact rating.

interventions.use_case: Meta-analysis of ChatGPT used as a learning aid in K-12 and college-like educational settings, including intelligent tutoring, conversational partner, tutoring support, assessment/feedback, and personalized recommendation across instructional models.

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT had a large positive overall effect on learning performance across 44 independent effects from 51 studies (g=0.867, 95% CI 0.683 to 1.052). The meta-analysis included experimental and quasi-experimental comparisons of ChatGPT-supported instruction versus standard non-ChatGPT instruction, with stronger effects in problem-based learning (g=1.113) and 4–8 week implementations (g=0.999).
finding.measure: Learning performance measured primarily through tests and exams
finding.study_size: k=44 independent effects (51 studies total; exact total N not reported in the summary table)

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT showed a moderate positive effect on learning perception across 19 independent effects (g=0.456, 95% CI 0.287 to 0.625). The effect was strongest for longer interventions, especially those lasting more than 8 weeks (g=1.054), suggesting sustained exposure improved students’ perceived learning experiences, attitudes, and related affective responses.
finding.measure: Learning perception measured primarily through scales and questionnaires

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking across 9 independent effects (g=0.457, 95% CI 0.255 to 0.650). Effects varied by course type and role: STEM and related courses showed the largest gains (g=0.737), and ChatGPT was most effective when used as an intelligent tutor (g=0.945).
finding.measure: Higher-order thinking measured primarily through scales and questionnaires
